🛡️ GUARD RAIL — do not repeat: NEVER run in-process V8 heap instrumentation against a hono-host (papercusp-bg-host :3271, :3070, :3170). The event-loop-sentinel SIGKILLs the host when the main thread blocks >=20s, and BOTH of these exceed it on a multi-GB heap — killing the process AND destroying the very heap you were measuring:
- HeapProfiler.takeHeapSnapshot — killed bg-host 03:22:15Z (2026-09-09), blocked 24s.
- Runtime.queryObjects — killed bg-host 04:03:23Z, blocked 24018ms, EVEN THOUGH a bare HeapProfiler.collectGarbage measured only 4301ms immediately before. Timing the GC does NOT bound queryObjects: the heap WALK, not the GC, is what wedges.
SAFE on the same process (measured, no kill): SIGUSR1 to open the inspector, and Runtime.evaluate of a short expression returning COUNTS/aggregates only (~2s).
Both kills were mine and both corrupted the bg-host death census on WI-10000804. Use out-of-process evidence (heap-sampling profiles in ~/.papercusp/heap-snapshots, pg_stat_statements deltas, /proc RSS sampling) instead.

ideas.title: Intent membrane for failing tools
ideas.body: The load-bearing assumption is that every agent must already know the exact, current argument schema before it can express a valid operation. The 87% sessions:read failure rate, invalid-escape self-tail failures, hidden structured completion schema, and live-cap rejection suggest this assumption is imposing protocol knowledge on every caller. I found no evidence in the digest of a universal runtime compatibility membrane; verify that an equivalent mechanism does not already exist before building it. Removing the assumption would let agents submit stable semantic intents while the platform evolves its wire contracts independently.
ideas.mechanism: Add an intent endpoint generated from the live tool registry. An intent contains operation name, semantic fields, caller contract fingerprint, and the original payload. The membrane resolves aliases and legacy shapes, clamps or negotiates live caps, parses escaped payloads losslessly, and either executes the canonical handler or returns a machine-readable repair plan with the exact normalized arguments. Successful repairs are stored as contract-versioned transformations, not silently applied forever. Instrument direct calls versus membrane calls, repair rate, semantic-preservation checks, and downstream completion rate; promote a transformation only after differential tests show identical handler meaning.

ideas.title: Proof capsules instead of evaluator trust
ideas.body: The silent assumption is that a terminal scorecard can trust the evaluator session that produced it to remain the authority for its own evidence. Remove that assumption: a grade becomes an executable claim that any independent verifier can replay, compare, and re-rate. This directly targets the measured weakness in grading-integrity instrument separation and the recurring gaps around missing spec pins, non-reproducible reruns, and judge access. It also avoids treating a passing current card as proof that its measurement instrument was independent.
ideas.mechanism: At scorecard creation, emit a self-contained proof capsule: immutable spec revision and fingerprint, evaluator-build digest, replay snapshot, exact input projection, instrument partition, oracle identity, and raw observations. The emitter cannot stamp terminal status unless a separate verifier process replays the capsule and produces a signed result; the verifier must use a different code path and explicitly reject shared fixtures or author-owned observations. Store both original and verifier verdicts, and make terminal-re-rate compare them rather than rerunning an unpinned recipe. Measure disagreement rate, replay success, and the fraction of cards whose evidence remains valid after evaluator upgrades.

ideas.title: Federation without a live outbox
ideas.body: The load-bearing assumption is that cross-hive coordination is a push conversation: papercusp must keep a live outbox drained by a responsive peer. The repeated 2869-second outbox stall and peer-federation silence show the cost of making liveness part of delivery. I found no evidence in the digest of a durable pull-based anti-entropy channel; verify before building. If that assumption is false, federation can progress while peers are silent, restarted, or temporarily unable to invoke coordination tools.
ideas.mechanism: Replace delivery dependence on peer sessions with signed append-only federation segments addressed by content hash. A sender seals a segment locally and publishes its hash through any available durable substrate; peers periodically pull missing segments, verify sequence/tenant/signature, apply idempotently, and acknowledge a vector watermark. A repair worker compares watermarks and reconstructs missing ranges rather than opening a fresh escalation per stalled row. Keep push as a latency optimization only. Measure time-to-durable-publication separately from peer-ack latency, missing-range repair rate, duplicate application rate, and whether 2869-second stalls still block useful work.

## Idea (lens: constraint-removal)
Title: Federation without a live outbox

What it is:
The load-bearing assumption is that cross-hive coordination is a push conversation: papercusp must keep a live outbox drained by a responsive peer. ## Idea (lens: constraint-removal)
Title: Intent membrane for failing tools

What it is:
The load-bearing assumption is that every agent must already know the exact, current argument schema before it can express a valid operation. The 87% sessions:read failure rate, invalid-escape self-tail failures, hidden structured completion schema, and live-cap rejection suggest this assumption is imposing protocol knowledge on every caller. I found no evidence in the digest of a universal runtime compatibility membrane; verify that an equivalent mechanism does not already exist before building it. Removing the assumption would let agents submit stable semantic intents while the platform evolves its wire contracts independently.

Proposed mechanism:
Add an intent endpoint generated from the live tool registry. An intent contains operation name, semantic fields, caller contract fingerprint, and the original payload. The membrane resolves aliases and legacy shapes, clamps or negotiates live caps, parses escaped payloads losslessly, and either executes the canonical handler or returns a machine-readable repair plan with the exact normalized arguments. Successful repairs are stored as contract-versioned transformations, not silently applied forever. Instrument direct calls versus membrane calls, repair rate, semantic-preservation checks, and downstream completion rate; promote a transformation only after differential tests show identical handler meaning.

🛡️ GUARD RAIL — do not repeat: NEVER run in-process V8 heap instrumentation against a hono-host (papercusp-bg-host :3271, :3070, :3170). The event-loop-sentinel SIGKILLs the host when the main thread blocks >=20s, and BOTH of these exceed it on a multi-GB heap — killing the process AND destroying the very heap you were measuring:
- HeapProfiler.takeHeapSnapshot — killed bg-host 03:22:15Z (2026-09-09), blocked 24s.
- Runtime.queryObjects — killed bg-host 04:03:23Z, blocked 24018ms, EVEN THOUGH a bare HeapProfiler.collectGarbage measured only 4301ms immediately before. Timing the GC does NOT bound queryObjects: the heap WALK, not the GC, is what wedges.
SAFE on the same process (measured, no kill): SIGUSR1 to open the inspector, and Runtime.evaluate of a short expression returning COUNTS/aggregates only (~2s).
Both kills were mine and both corrupted the bg-host death census on WI-10000804. Use out-of-process evidence (heap-sampling profiles in ~/.papercusp/heap-snapshots, pg_stat_statements deltas, /proc RSS sampling) instead.

ideas.title: Intent Capsules Instead of Tool Calls
ideas.body: The load-bearing assumption is that an agent must know and emit the exact current MCP schema to perform work. Make that false: agents submit a semantic intent capsule (operation, entity, desired effect, and observed context), while a gateway resolves the versioned contract, translates aliases, fills safe defaults, and returns an ambiguity question only when multiple mappings remain. I found no evidence in the digest that a universal intent-to-contract resolver already exists; verify before building. This could turn repeated invalid_input and validator failures from agent-level dead ends into compatibility events, while preserving the original intent for audit rather than silently guessing.
ideas.mechanism: Define a versioned intent envelope with operation, named semantic fields, expected postcondition, and optional failed-call payload. The gateway selects the deployed tool schema, validates and normalizes the envelope, executes once, and returns a receipt containing canonical arguments, schema fingerprint, result, or a machine-readable ambiguity set. Learn mappings only from explicitly accepted corrections; never infer destructive fields. Add contract-conformance probes that replay recent failures for sessions:read, work_items:complete, scorecards:get, and plans:get-spec-evidence, measuring first-attempt success, clarification rate, and semantic-equivalence of the resulting action. This is a new execution/knowledge niche, not another retry wrapper.

ideas.title: Evidence Objects, Not Evidence Prose
ideas.body: The silent assumption is that grading evidence is authored as prose and later interpreted by an evaluator. Remove it: a proof should be an executable, immutable object whose prose is merely a rendered view. This directly targets the recurring failure where valid evidence embeds re-run arguments that the deployed evaluator rejects, and prevents future drift between what was executed and what is claimed. I found no evidence that every evidence string is currently generated from the stored recipe; verify before building.
ideas.mechanism: Make plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy and plans:bind-spec-evidence accept a proof object containing canonical tool name, schema fingerprint, exact args, fixture/test fingerprints, mutation or counterexample, oracle declaration, execution result, and environment scope. The service executes or verifies that object, stores its hash, and generates the human-readable attestation and re-run command from the same canonical args object; free-form evidence becomes commentary only. A compatibility renderer can convert legacy prose into a quarantined unverified object, never a pass. Add a mutation test that changes rendered prose while holding the object fixed, and a tamper test that changes args while holding prose fixed; both must expose the mismatch. Report first-attempt evaluator acceptance and object/prose divergence, explicitly preserving the current base-rate and instrument-split checks.

## Idea (lens: constraint-removal)
Title: Intent Capsules Instead of Tool Calls

What it is:
The load-bearing assumption is that an agent must know and emit the exact current MCP schema to perform work. Make that false: agents submit a semantic intent capsule (operation, entity, desired effect, and observed context), while a gateway resolves the versioned contract, translates aliases, fills safe defaults, and returns an ambiguity question only when multiple mappings remain. I found no evidence in the digest that a universal intent-to-contract resolver already exists; verify before building. This could turn repeated invalid_input and validator failures from agent-level dead ends into compatibility events, while preserving the original intent for audit rather than silently guessing.

Proposed mechanism:
Define a versioned intent envelope with operation, named semantic fields, expected postcondition, and optional failed-call payload. The gateway selects the deployed tool schema, validates and normalizes the envelope, executes once, and returns a receipt containing canonical arguments, schema fingerprint, result, or a machine-readable ambiguity set. Learn mappings only from explicitly accepted corrections; never infer destructive fields. Add contract-conformance probes that replay recent failures for sessions:read, work_items:complete, scorecards:get, and plans:get-spec-evidence, measuring first-attempt success, clarification rate, and semantic-equivalence of the resulting action. This is a new execution/knowledge niche, not another retry wrapper.

## Idea (lens: constraint-removal)
Title: Evidence Objects, Not Evidence Prose

What it is:
The silent assumption is that grading evidence is authored as prose and later interpreted by an evaluator. Remove it: a proof should be an executable, immutable object whose prose is merely a rendered view. This directly targets the recurring failure where valid evidence embeds re-run arguments that the deployed evaluator rejects, and prevents future drift between what was executed and what is claimed. I found no evidence that every evidence string is currently generated from the stored recipe; verify before building.

Proposed mechanism:
Make plans:evaluate-spec-test-adequacy and plans:bind-spec-evidence accept a proof object containing canonical tool name, schema fingerprint, exact args, fixture/test fingerprints, mutation or counterexample, oracle declaration, execution result, and environment scope. The service executes or verifies that object, stores its hash, and generates the human-readable attestation and re-run command from the same canonical args object; free-form evidence becomes commentary only. A compatibility renderer can convert legacy prose into a quarantined unverified object, never a pass. Add a mutation test that changes rendered prose while holding the object fixed, and a tamper test that changes args while holding prose fixed; both must expose the mismatch. Report first-attempt evaluator acceptance and object/prose divergence, explicitly preserving the current base-rate and instrument-split checks.
